title: Thin Plate
comment: Thin Plate — Thin plate spline is one of the most popular data interpolation methods. Its solution can be written in 2D using the r^2 log(r) radial basis function. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thin_plate_spline#cite_note-Duchon76-1
alt_text: Thin Plate. Thin plate spline is one of the most popular data interpolation methods. Its solution can be written in 2D using the r^2 log(r) radial basis function.

comment: Discretization Measure — Lagrangian discretization of measures: quotient space. Eulerian discretization: convex polytope.

title: Pendulum Oscilator
comment: Pendulum Oscilator — The damped harmonic oscillator (linear) vs simple gravity pendulum (non-linear). The two most celebrated second order dynamical systems. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmonic_oscillator
alt_text: Pendulum Oscilator. The damped harmonic oscillator (linear) vs simple gravity pendulum (non-linear). The two most celebrated second order dynamical systems.

title: Iterative Projections
comment: Iterative Projections — Iterative projections: converge in theory for convex sets. Works great in practice for non-convex sets. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projections_onto_convex_sets
alt_text: Iterative Projections. Iterative projections: converge in theory for convex sets. Works great in practice for non-convex sets.

title: Proximal Operator
comment: Proximal Operator — The proximal operator is the implicit counterpart of the explicit gradient descent step. Fundamental to tackle non-smooth optimization problems. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximal_operator
alt_text: Proximal Operator. The proximal operator is the implicit counterpart of the explicit gradient descent step. Fundamental to tackle non-smooth optimization problems.

title: Sgd
comment: Sgd — Stochastic gradient method: works also for infinite sums and expectation. Introduced by Herbert Robbins and Sutton Monro. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stochastic_approximation
alt_text: Sgd. Stochastic gradient method: works also for infinite sums and expectation. Introduced by Herbert Robbins and Sutton Monro.

title: Aniso Diffusion
comment: Aniso Diffusion — Tensor-driven anisotropic diffusion solves the heat equation on a manifold defined by a tensor field. At the heart of many methods for image restauration, texture enhancement and vizualization. The book of Joachim Weickert i… https://www.mia.uni-saarland.de/weickert/Papers/book.pdf
alt_text: Aniso Diffusion. Tensor-driven anisotropic diffusion solves the heat equation on a manifold defined by a tensor field. At the heart of many methods for image restauration, texture enhancement and vizualization. The book of Joachim Weickert is a must read.

title: Power Iter Convergence
comment: Power Iter Convergence — Power iterations do not converge for matrices with multiple complex eigenvalues with same maximum modulus. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_iteration
alt_text: Power Iter Convergence. Power iterations do not converge for matrices with multiple complex eigenvalues with same maximum modulus.

title: Knn
comment: Knn — K-nearest neighbors is the baseline method for non-parametric classification. Computes an estimate of the relative density of the two classes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-nearest_neighbors_algorithm
alt_text: Knn. K-nearest neighbors is the baseline method for non-parametric classification. Computes an estimate of the relative density of the two classes.

title: Leapfrog
comment: Leapfrog — Leapfrog/Verlet are symplectic integrators which approximately conserve hamiltonian, preserve periodic behaviors and are exactly reversible. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leapfrog_integration
alt_text: Leapfrog. Leapfrog/Verlet are symplectic integrators which approximately conserve hamiltonian, preserve periodic behaviors and are exactly reversible.

title: Taylor Exp
comment: Taylor Exp — Taylor series of exp(it) up to degree 15. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_series
alt_text: Taylor Exp. Taylor series of exp(it) up to degree 15.

title: Heat Eq
comment: Heat Eq — The heat equation can be applied to diffuse probability densities (in particular, maintains positivity and unit mass). Its solution is obtained as the convolution of the initial condition with a Gaussian. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation
alt_text: Heat Eq. The heat equation can be applied to diffuse probability densities (in particular, maintains positivity and unit mass). Its solution is obtained as the convolution of the initial condition with a Gaussian.

title: Binomial
comment: Binomial — The binomial law is a sum of Bernoulli 0/1 random variables. After rescaling, converge to a Gaussian for a large number of variables (a particular case of the central limit theorem). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binomial_distribution
alt_text: Binomial. The binomial law is a sum of Bernoulli 0/1 random variables. After rescaling, converge to a Gaussian for a large number of variables (a particular case of the central limit theorem).

title: Convex Hull
comment: Convex Hull — The convex hull is the smallest enclosing convex set. It is also the intersection of all half-spaces containing the points, and the set of all possible convex combinations. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convex_hull
alt_text: Convex Hull. The convex hull is the smallest enclosing convex set. It is also the intersection of all half-spaces containing the points, and the set of all possible convex combinations.

title: Lin Dyn Systems
comment: Lin Dyn Systems — Behavior of dynamical system depends on the eigenvalues. In 2D it can be classified according to the trace and determinant. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stability_theory
alt_text: Lin Dyn Systems. Behavior of dynamical system depends on the eigenvalues. In 2D it can be classified according to the trace and determinant.

title: Self Org Maps
comment: Self Org Maps — Self-organizing maps of Kohonen defines a map between a 2D space to the data, by minimizing a quantization error and a regularity penalty. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-organizing_map
alt_text: Self Org Maps. Self-organizing maps of Kohonen defines a map between a 2D space to the data, by minimizing a quantization error and a regularity penalty.

title: Rbf
comment: Rbf — Radial basis functions performs interpolation and approximation by solving a linear system. In some cases (e.g. Gaussian and polyharmonic), corresponds to regression in a reproducing Hilbert space. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radial_basis_function
alt_text: Rbf. Radial basis functions performs interpolation and approximation by solving a linear system. In some cases (e.g. Gaussian and polyharmonic), corresponds to regression in a reproducing Hilbert space.

title: Lorentz Attractor
comment: Lorentz Attractor — Lorenz attractor is the set of limit trajectories for a simplified mathematical model for atmospheric convection. It has a fractal geometry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenz_system
alt_text: Lorentz Attractor. Lorenz attractor is the set of limit trajectories for a simplified mathematical model for atmospheric convection. It has a fractal geometry.
